To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed a computer vision approach that recognizes facial expressions using FACS action units and action unit combinations.

(1) facial action units can be automatically recognized from the upper face using HMMs; (2) the combination of facial feature point tracking and dense flow tracking is more accurate than using only feature point tracking or only dense flow tracking; (3) high accuracy of recognition of upper face expressions can be achieved by using HMMs to combine feature point tracking and high gradient component (furrow) detection.

the use of a combination of three approaches to extract upper face expression information results in a 95% recognition rate for the six basic expressions (anger, disgust, fear, joy, sadness, and surprise).
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing an automated system to recognize facial expressions using FACS action units.
the development of a system for the automated recognition of facial expression using the FACS action unit coding system.
the development of a computer vision system capable of automatically recognizing facial expressions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
dense flow tracking is the most effective method to recognize upper face expressions.
the dense flow tracking method is the most accurate method to extract upper face expressions.
the use of dense flow tracking and PCA is a very promising approach to the automated recognition of upper face expressions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our approach to facial expression is based on the FACS, which separates expressions into the upper and lower face actions.
the use of HMMs and FACS is a good approach for automated facial expression recognition.
our approach to facial expression analysis is robust to different lighting conditions, and that it can automatically detect facial expression in real-time.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of dense flow tracking and high gradient component tracking is the most effective approach.
the use of high gradient components (i.e., high gradient component detection) is a viable approach to facial expression analysis.
facial expression recognition can be achieved with high accuracy using HMMs.
